newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: KIDNAPPED S.AFRICAN BABY FOUND IN MALAWI.
newsitem.headline: KIDNAPPED S.AFRICAN BABY FOUND IN MALAWI.

text.p: A South African tug-of-love baby, kidnapped from its adoptive parents in Malawi on Saturday, was found in a ditch by two village boys early on Tuesday, police said.
"The child was found on a river bank...by two boys, who reported it to their village chief," South African police detective Sharon Schutte told Reuters.

"The chief summoned the police and he was taken to a doctor for medical tests. The baby was covered in mosquito bites but is healthy and unharmed and back with its (adoptive) parents," she said, adding that police had no information on the kidnappers.
Soon after Timothy Funnell was reported missing on Saturday, police issued an alert and photographs of the 14-month-old baby.
Timothy's birth mother, classical musician Adri Naude, said over the weekend the boy was kidnapped by two men who ran off with him into the mountains around Malawi's Blantyre.

"I don't care what anybody does to me but leave my child alone," Naude said on Saturday. "I will kill whoever is involved in this thing. I really feel very strongly about it and they must not do anything to harm my baby at all."

The child's birth father, Laurie Fraser, has waged a lengthy court battle for the right to raise his son as a single father. Their marriage plans went awry and Naude later agreed to their baby's adoption without his consent.
Fraser went to South Africa's most powerful judicial authority, the 11-judge Constitutional Court, to try and gain the right to raise his son.

The court ruled in a landmark decision that single fathers should be allowed to have a say in their children's adoptions and gave legislators two years to introduce it into law. Fraser is now fighting for custody in the Supreme Court.
